text: Volatile Shadow was planned to be a shadow elemental crafting reagent in . However, it didn't make it out of beta. In an official overview on professions in Cataclysm, this item was described as a drop from mining obsidian, which was was presumably an earlier name for obsidium.

Volrath's Advance is a subzone of Ashran, and the north-central Tower of the Road of Glory. A curving path leads north up to the Emberfall Tower, while directly to the south lies the open plains of The Crossroads. A smaller path leads east to The Dark Woods. Situated directly in the shadow of Emberfall Tower, the Warspear Tower Guardian Jeron Emberfall watches over the Advance, casting summoned phoenixes to explode upon the heads of attackers below. The second Horde Tower in the zone, all Horde players within Volrath's Advance gain 10% to their healing and damage done.

Volund's Hoard is a tomb for Warlord Volund within the Tomb of the Old Kings on Shield's Rest in Stormheim. An adventurer journeys here with Grif Wildheart and Prustaga to obtain Titanstrike. After disabling the room's runes and defeating the robotic defenses, an Image of Mimiron deactivates the security measures hiding Titanstrike, but Volund's spirit materializes to stop them. After a brief fight, Prustaga stuns everyone, claims the weapon and disappears through a portal.

The Voldunai is a faction of vulpera and Zandalari exiles found in Vol'dun. "Voldunai" seems to be a general name for most non-hostile, non-sethrak inhabitants of Vol'dun, encompassing everything from vulpera caravans and the worshippers of Akunda, to individual groups of Zandalari like those at the Goldtusk Inn and the Scorched Sands Outpost. Alabaster hyenas are used by the Voldunai to quickly move unseen throughout the sands.
Volatile Rats are rats located in Millstone Hamlet in Stormsong Valley.

Volatile Bubbles are located at Fizzsprings Resort in Tiragarde Sound. Disturbing them will cause a number of Gelatinous Sulfurs to spawn.
Volni's Skull is looted from Volni in the Sandfury Hideout in Vol'dun.

__NOTOC__ The Voru'kar are an uncorrupted group of nerubians located on Skittering Hollow. Their leader, Vorus'arak led them safely away from the Lich King during The War of The Spider. Their vizier, Prophet Nox'tir, claims that the invaders of their home will never find their hidden egg cache.

Vorrik is one of the Keepers, a trio of sethrak responsible for protecting Mythrax the Unraveler's tomb of Atul'Aman, and once co-ruled the sethrak with his fellow Keeper Korthek. When Korthek betrayed his duty as a Keeper, declared himself emperor, and sought to unleash Mythrax to conquer Zandalar, Vorrik and his followers — known as the Devoted — remained loyal to their loa Sethraliss and have been fighting Korthek's Faithless ever since.

Vorrik's Keystone is one of three keystones that were created by the sethrak Keepers to maintain the barrier around Atul'Aman. Vorrik initially stores the keystone in the topmost chamber of the Sanctuary of the Devoted in Vol'dun, but it's later stolen by the troops of General Jakra'zet along with Sulthis' Keystone.
The Voldunai Commendation is automatically consumed and provides the amount of reputation shown in its tooltip with the Voldunai.

__NOTOC__ Vorrik's Sanctum is a cave on the northern slopes of the Crackling Ridge, south of the Crater of Conquerors in Vol'dun. The entrance is located underneath a huge, hollowed-out dead tree. Years ago, the sethrak Vorrik used the cave as his personal sanctum and as a shrine to Sethraliss where he could meditate, until he was forced to abandon it due to Korthek's betrayal. However, it is currently inhabited by vulpera who are fighting the Faithless sethrak and rescuing vulpera slaves. Upon discovering this, Vorrik states that, while it's unconventional, he believes Sethraliss would be pleased to see her shrine used to protect innocents in need. The Volumes of Victory are the single most important compendium of Maldraxxus military history ever assembled, and the most famous of all the writings stored in Maldraxxus' Sepulcher of Knowledge. According to the broker Ta'eran, the book is almost literally priceless. The work is split up into a seemingly endless number of volumes (at least 583 ones), all stored in the hidden library under the Sepulcher. Ta'eran enlisted Maw Walkers to help him collect as many of the volumes as possible while also stating that he would have to prepare a larger expedition to collect the rest of the volumes at a later point.

The Vul'Gol Ogre Mound is a small basin in southern Duskwood, which is completely overrun by Splinter Fist ogres led by Zzarc'Vul, after which the mound was named. It is located just to the southwest of where the main road through Duskwood splits and runs south into Stranglethorn Vale. As the Night Watch wanted to only risk its few members in the defense of more immediate threats, they engaged adventurers to come here and kill some of the ogres in exchange for rewards. At some point, the necromancer Abercrombie was attacked by the Splinter Fist ogres who stole his "crate of precious tools and herbs" and brought it to their mound. He later sent an Alliance adventurer to recover the crate. Vik

Vultures are carrion birds that can be found throughout the drier areas of Kalimdor — seeking carnage upon which to feed. The mottled scavengers have been known to aid the vile harpies from time to time — drawn by the promise of freshly slain flesh and blood. They have also been seen in Outland, but with two heads. Boulderfist clan legend recounts a cloud of carrion birds following ogre warriors through the Dark Portal during the Second War; it may be that all two-headed scavengers in Azeroth are their descendants. Mulgore swoops are often hunted for their quills by the tauren.
Vosh'gajin's Strand was a quest reward from Warlord's Command and Maxwell's Mission.

He has two NPCs based off of him in-game - Skycaller Vrakthris, and Brock Thriss.

Vulraiis is a massive smith's hammer used by the titan Khaz'goroth the Shaper. He crafted this enormous hammer from ultrapure thorium, after which Aman'Thul and Norgannon worked together to enchant it. The hammer's appearance suggests a smith's tool more than a weapon, and indeed Khaz'goroth uses it at his forge. When he wields it in combat, however, it causes great seismic eruptions and splitting earthquakes.

The Vote Kick system was introduced in patch 3.3 with the Dungeon Finder Tools. It can be used to remove a player when a majority of the group as a whole believes that replacing the player is in the best interests of the dungeon group. Using the Vote Kick feature too often will not allow a player to initiate a Vote Kick for 2 hours.

The Vrykul Rune Stick is an archaeology keystone. It acts as 12 pieces of Vrykul Archaeology Fragments in research on Vrykul archaeology finds that have 'sockets'.

W!Zone is an add-on pack to the highly popular game Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness. It is the first "W!Zone" add-on, released before W!Zone II Retribution. It offers 66 "completely new, custom-designed battlegrounds," which contain ten single-player maps, 33 two-player maps, one three-player map, eight four-player maps, one five-player map, one seven-player map, and six eight-player maps.
W!Zone II Retribution is an add-on pack to the highly popular game Warcraft II: Tides of Darkness. It is the second "W!Zone" add-on, released after W!Zone.
Vrykul drinking Horn is a rare archaeology artifact that requires 100 Vrykul Archaeology Fragments to solve. Up to three Vrykul Rune Stick keystones may be used to complete it.
